name: no-non-null-assertion
description: Disallow the non-null assertion `x!` in production code — it tells the compiler a value exists without proving it, so the proof the compiler would have demanded never gets written. Test files are exempt: there a failed assumption throws and fails the test, which is the assertion's purpose.
fixHint: Prove the value exists: destructure with a guard (`const [first] = xs; if (first === undefined) return …`), use `.at()`/`.find()` and narrow, or restructure so the type already excludes null/undefined.
